problem: It says 172.16.0.0/12 is wrongly seen as "three separate class B networks". The count is wrong: /12 covers 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255, which is 16 class B (/16) networks, not three. The rest of the trap (one prefix, mask 255.240.0.0) is right, so the wrong number teaches a false fact.
fix: Treating 172.16.0.0/12 as a single class B network. It is one private prefix covering 16 class B networks, 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255; its mask is 255.240.0.0.

problem: "0.0.0.0 means this host or any address in a routing table" is too compressed. A student may not see that the meaning depends on where the address appears (source address versus routing-table entry).
fix: 0.0.0.0 used as a source address means this host, before it knows its own address; in a routing table it is the default route, matching any destination.

problem: The Hosts note ".4.1 to .7.254" is written as octet fragments with no full address, so on a phone it reads like a different network from the one in the same figure.
fix: Use the full range in the note: 172.16.4.1 to 172.16.7.254.
